title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: Each of \(20\) balls is tossed independently and at random into one of \(5\) bins. Let \(p\) be the probability that some bin ends up with \(3\) balls, another with \(5\) balls, and the other three with \(4\) balls each. Let \(q\) be the probability that every bin ends up with \(4\) balls. What is \(\dfrac{p}{q}?\)

solutions.text:
Both probabilities divide by \(5^{20},\) so \(\dfrac{p}{q}\) is a ratio of arrangement counts.

For \(q,\) all bins have \(4:\) \(\dfrac{20!}{(4!)^5}.\) For \(p,\) choose which bin has \(3\) and which has \(5\) in \(5\cdot 4 = 20\) ways, times \(\dfrac{20!}{3!\,5!\,(4!)^3}.\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{p}{q} &= 20 \cdot \frac{(4!)^5}{3!\,5!\,(4!)^3} \\ &= 20 \cdot \frac{(4!)^2}{3!\,5!} \\ &= 20 \cdot \frac{576}{720} \\ &= 16. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Both probabilities share the same \(5^{20}\) denominator, so \(\dfrac{p}{q}\) is a ratio of counts
\(q\) uses \(\dfrac{20!}{(4!)^5};\) \(p\) uses \(5\cdot 4\) choices of the special bins times \(\dfrac{20!}{3!\,5!\,(4!)^3}\)
